The exact minimal real-linear Lipschitz amplification is a naturally defined Banach extension invariant, not implied by nonlinear scalar extension existence. Three independent dihedral orbit weights equioscillate the vertex constraints; a positive convolution simultaneously controls every midpoint pair. The strict improvement over arithmetic interpolation is mathematical structure relevant to stable finite geometric interpolation, despite the intentionally finite scope.
